note: Unselected T2D; three CCR2 antagonists (CCX140-B/ilacirnon, JNJ-41443532, BMS-741672) reached 4-12-week Phase 2 on the DIO-mouse adipose-macrophage hypothesis and none went further in diabetes.
label: Type 2 diabetes (CCR2)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMC open access). The antagonist is not named in the abstract and is not a member; product_in_model false. Weisberg opener stands for the JNJ-41443532 track (proxy source; no JNJ-41443532 model paper exists).
engagement.model: Diet-induced obese / db/db mice dosed with a CCR2 antagonist
engagement.note: Weisberg 2006: a CCR2 antagonist cut adipose-tissue macrophage content in obese mice; that readout was never measured in dosed patients.
engagement.short: CCR2 blockade cleared adipose macrophages in mice
engagement.quote: In mice with established obesity, short-term treatment with a pharmacological antagonist of CCR2 lowered macrophage content of adipose tissue and improved insulin sensitivity without significantly altering body mass or improving hepatic steatosis.

engagement.confidence_note: Registry results record; the Di Prospero 2014 full text (Wiley) returned 403 so any monocyte or CCL2 pharmacodynamics in the paper could not be checked.
engagement.judgement: Left untested rather than scored on systemic IL-6/CRP: the mouse readout was adipose-tissue macrophage content, which no member trial measured. The CCX140-B press release reports only that monocytes and MCP-1 did not change, which is a selectivity claim, not engagement; it is scored under safety on the hCCR2 knock-in track. No member was ever filed, so model_filed is null for the class.
engagement.model: Diet-induced obese / db/db mice dosed with a CCR2 antagonist
engagement.note: JNJ-41443532 and CCX140-B trials reported no adipose-macrophage, occupancy or CCL2 engagement readout in T2D patients; IL-6, IL-18 and CRP did not move. Adds the first patient-side look: no member trial measured the mouse's readout.
engagement.short: Model PD readout never measured in patients
engagement.quote: Change From Baseline to Day 28 in Systemic Levels of Interleukin 6 (IL-6)
engagement.reason: PD readout of the mouse never measured in patients

dose.model: Diet-induced obese / db/db mice dosed with a CCR2 antagonist
dose.note: Weisberg 2006 dosed an unnamed CCR2 antagonist short-term in obese mice; no exposure or occupancy target was stated for humans.
dose.short: No exposure target stated by the mouse
dose.quote: In mice with established obesity, short-term treatment with a pharmacological antagonist of CCR2 lowered macrophage content of adipose tissue and improved insulin sensitivity without significantly altering body mass or improving hepatic steatosis.

dose.confidence_note: Full text read through PMC. The ChemoCentryx release says only 'excellent plasma coverage'; Di Prospero 2014 gives PK (tmax 2 h, t1/2 8 h) but no occupancy or target, and the 1000 mg arm did no better than 250 mg.
dose.judgement: Dose stays untested on both tracks: no source states the exposure the mice needed against what patients reached. The hCCR2 knock-in work was published two years after the clinical T2D result it cites (a retrodiction on the efficacy and safety cells); here it is unscored, so retrodiction is left false to satisfy decision 10's scored-entry rule.
dose.model: Human-CCR2 knock-in DIO / db/db mice dosed with CCX140-B
dose.note: hCCR2 knock-in mice: 30 mg/kg gave a 170 nM trough near the 200 nM chemotaxis IC50, glycaemia needed 100 mg/kg; the paper makes no human exposure comparison and the sponsor gave no numbers.
dose.short: Mouse trough 170 nM; no human comparison
dose.quote: The trough plasma level of CCX140 in mice treated with 30 mg/kg CCX140-B was 170 nM.
dose.reason: No stated target; 1000 mg JNJ no better than 250 mg

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (PMC open access). Weisberg opener stands for the ilacirnon (CCX140-B) track (proxy source).
efficacy.model: Diet-induced obese / db/db mice dosed with a CCR2 antagonist
efficacy.note: CCR2 knockout and a short-term CCR2 antagonist improved insulin sensitivity and glucose homeostasis in high-fat-fed mice; no patient data yet.
efficacy.short: CCR2 blockade improved insulin sensitivity in DIO mice
efficacy.quote: In obese mice matched for adiposity, Ccr2 deficiency reduced macrophage content and the inflammatory profile of adipose tissue, increased adiponectin expression, ameliorated hepatic steatosis, and improved systemic glucose homeostasis and insulin sensitivity.

efficacy.confidence_note: Tier 5: sponsor press release (15 Sep 2011) of an EASD 2011 presentation (Hanefeld). NCT01028963 never posted results and the Hanefeld 2012 J Diabetes Metab paper could not be located in PubMed, so the per-arm numbers (HbA1c -0.09 placebo, -0.09 5 mg, -0.23 10 mg, -0.13 pioglitazone, from conference coverage) are unverified.
efficacy.judgement: The trial's registered primary endpoint was adverse-event incidence; fasting glucose/HbA1c was the proof-of-concept gate, hence poc_gate. Scored same because the direction matched the mouse for one member, but the effect is a 0.14-point HbA1c separation at 4 weeks with no effect at 5 mg, and ChemoCentryx then moved the drug to diabetic nephropathy rather than a T2D Phase 2b. Paired by the drafter against Weisberg 2006; the JPET 2012 CCX140-B pharmacology paper was retracted (compound identity undisclosed) and is not used. No member was ever filed, so model_filed is null for the class.
efficacy.model: Diet-induced obese / db/db mice dosed with a CCR2 antagonist
efficacy.note: CCX140-B 10 mg for 4 weeks on metformin: HbA1c fell vs placebo (p=0.045), 5 mg did not; fasting glucose fell dose-dependently. Small, direction only. Add-on to metformin in every arm, placebo-controlled: not a combination trial.
efficacy.short: CCX140-B 10 mg lowered HbA1c at 4 weeks
efficacy.quote: A significant decrease in HbA1c was observed after only 4 weeks of daily treatment of CCX140-B (10 mg) compared to placebo (p = 0.045).

patient_trials.quote: Randomized subjects received double-blind placebo QD, 5 mg CCX140-B QD, 10 mg CCX140-B QD, or open label pioglitazone hydrochloride 30 mg for 4 weeks.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: placebo-adjusted 24-h weighted mean glucose; HOMA-IR, which the mice normalised, did not move
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract plus the ClinicalTrials.gov results record (primary 24-h WAG: pioglitazone -27.4, 250 mg -20.5 p=0.038, 1000 mg -13.2 p=0.178 mg/dL vs placebo; HOMA-IR 250 mg -0.26 p=0.77). Full text paywalled (403).
efficacy.judgement: Kept at same with source_calls_it partial rather than contra: the primary endpoint did respond in the predicted direction at 250 mg, which the v3 rule scores as a match with magnitude recorded. The case for contra is real: no dose response, HOMA-IR (the mouse's mechanism readout) unchanged, half the pioglitazone effect, and all three sponsors abandoned the class in T2D. BMS-741672's 12-week HbA1c trial (NCT00699790, completed 2009) was never reported anywhere found, so it adds no status. No member was ever filed, so model_filed is null for the class.
efficacy.model: Diet-induced obese / db/db mice dosed with a CCR2 antagonist
efficacy.note: JNJ-41443532 4-week PoC: 24-h glucose -20 mg/dL vs placebo at 250 mg bid (p=0.038), -13 at 1000 mg (ns); HOMA-IR unchanged; sponsor called it modest and stopped. Second member, tier 1 with registry results; direction held, HOMA-IR did not.
efficacy.short: JNJ-41443532: modest glucose fall, no dose response
efficacy.quote: Administration of JNJ-41443532 resulted in modest improvement in glycaemic parameters compared with placebo, and was generally well tolerated in patients with T2DM.
efficacy.reason: Glucose fell a little; insulin sensitivity did not

patient_trials.quote: After 4 weeks, reductions in 23-h WMG and FPG were observed in all treatment groups compared with placebo and were significantly lower for 250-mg JNJ-41443532 and pioglitazone.
The purpose of the study is to determine whether a CCR2 antagonist (BMS-741672) improves glucose homeostasis in drug-naive type 2 diabetic patients

efficacy.magnitude_basis: fasting glucose direction; mouse HOMA-IR normalised versus a 0.14-point HbA1c separation in patients
efficacy.confidence_note: Sponsor-authored (ChemoCentryx). The paper states the clinical reduction in HbA1c and fasting glucose and reports the mouse glycaemic data alongside, so comparison_stated is true; the human numbers it cites are the unverified Hanefeld presentation.
efficacy.judgement: Scored retro, not same: the knock-in model was generated for CCX140-B and its glycaemic data appeared (received June 2013) after the September 2011 clinical result the paper itself cites, so by decision 10 it reproduces a known answer. No prospective prediction from this model followed in T2D; its later use was diabetic nephropathy (a different disease, not scored here). The Metabolism 2013 companion paper used a mouse-active analogue in DIO/db/db mice and is a sibling of the Weisberg track, not a new system. Rule question settled (2026-11-09): retro admits partial agreement exactly as same does; glucose direction reproduced (CCX140-B HbA1c, JNJ-41443532 24-h glucose), HOMA-IR and fasting insulin not, so retro with source_calls_it partial, not contra.
efficacy.model: Human-CCR2 knock-in DIO / db/db mice dosed with CCX140-B
efficacy.note: hCCR2 knock-in DIO mice built because CCX140-B does not bind mouse CCR2: fasting glucose and insulin fell, HOMA-IR normalised, published two years after the clinical HbA1c result it cites. Ruling: glucose reproduced, HOMA-IR not, so retro, partial.
efficacy.short: Knock-in mouse reproduced the clinical glucose fall
efficacy.quote: Moreover, treatment of diet-induced obese mice with CCX140-B resulted in decreased levels of fasting blood glucose and insulin, normalization of homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance values, and decreased numbers of adipose tissue inflammatory macrophages.

efficacy.confidence_note: CSR synopsis CL004_140 v1.0 (17 Mar 2011), posted to EU CTR 2022-03-01, read in full via pdftotext. The synopsis does not name the variant; the ClinicalTrials.gov record (NCT01028963) does not mention the stratification at all.
efficacy.judgement: First use of a human genetic stratifier for the class: the sponsor randomised within strata of MCP-1 polymorphism status, presumably the CCL2 -2518A/G promoter variant whose G allele lowers plasma MCP-1 and T2D prevalence (Simeoni 2004, doi:10.1007/s00125-004-1494-4). Patient-level, because the question is whether genotype predicts response to CCX140-B, not whether the class works. Opened at the trial's start (29 Jan 2010) with the 2022 registry posting as proxy source; product_in_model true because the member drug was dosed to the genotyped patients.
efficacy.model: T2D patients genotyped for an MCP-1 (CCL2) promoter polymorphism, used as a randomisation stratifier in the CCX140-B trial
efficacy.note: CCX140-B 4-week T2D trial (CL004_140, Jan-Nov 2010) randomised patients within strata of MCP-1 polymorphism status; genotype-by-response was a stated objective.
efficacy.short: Trial stratified by MCP-1 genotype; no result yet
efficacy.quote: Eligible subjects were stratified based on MCP-1 polymorphism status as well as gender.

efficacy.confidence_note: The synopsis (full read) reports FPG, HbA1c, HOMA-IR, insulin, OGTT, adiponectin, MCP-1 and hsCRP by arm and nothing by genotype. Whether the EASD 2011 presentation or Hanefeld 2012 J Diabetes Metab (not locatable in PubMed or at OMICS) reported the genotype analysis could not be checked; the 15 Sep 2011 press release does not mention it.
efficacy.judgement: Stays untested: the sponsor stated the genotype-by-response objective and never published its result anywhere found, so there is no comparison to score. Not trial_unreported, because the trial itself is reported at tier 3; only the stratifier analysis is missing. An unreported stratifier is not a contra. Dated 2022, the first time the objective and the stratification were public.

efficacy.note: CSR synopsis posted to EU CTR (Mar 2022) lists 'Assessment of MCP-1 polymorphism on efficacy responses' as an objective and reports no genotype result. Adds the patient-side look: the genotype objective existed and no result was ever published.
efficacy.quote: Assessment of MCP-1 polymorphism on efficacy responses to CCX140-B treatment.

safety.model: Diet-induced obese / db/db mice dosed with a CCR2 antagonist
safety.note: Weisberg 2006 states no harm; the one negative it reports is no change in body mass. No tolerability prediction to compare.
safety.quote: In mice with established obesity, short-term treatment with a pharmacological antagonist of CCR2 lowered macrophage content of adipose tissue and improved insulin sensitivity without significantly altering body mass or improving hepatic steatosis.

safety.magnitude_basis: blood monocyte count and plasma CCL2/MCP-1, unchanged in both
safety.confidence_note: Patient side is a sponsor press release (tier 5, no numbers); model side is Sullivan 2013 (Unlike other CCR2 antagonists, CCX140-B had no effect on plasma levels of the CCR2 ligand CCL2 or on the numbers of blood monocytes.). Year is 2013, when the mouse side became public; the press release is 2011.
safety.judgement: The only stated safety prediction on any track is the knock-in mouse's claim that CCX140-B spares circulating monocytes, and the model was published after the clinical observation, so retro by decision 10. Infection risk from CCR2 blockade, the class harm, was not predicted by either mouse and did not appear in 4-week trials; neither is a comparison. JNJ-41443532 and BMS-741672 have no published model-side safety statement. No member was ever filed, so model_filed is null for the class.
safety.model: Human-CCR2 knock-in DIO / db/db mice dosed with CCX140-B
safety.note: Knock-in mice: CCX140-B left blood monocytes and plasma CCL2 unchanged, unlike other CCR2 antagonists; the 2011 T2D trial had reported no monocyte or MCP-1 effect. Model after clinic.
safety.short: No monocytopenia: mouse and patients agree, retrodicted
safety.quote: No detrimental effects were observed on plasma MCP-1 or blood monocyte levels, and once daily oral CCX140-B provided excellent plasma coverage.
safety.reason: Mouse matched patients, but only after the fact
